Asturian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • cudiar
  • cuidiar (Allande)
  • coidar (archaic)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin cogitāre.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /kwiˈdaɾ/ [kwiˈð̞aɾ]
  • Rhymes: -aɾ
  • Syllabification: cui‧dar

Verb

[edit]

cuidar (first-person singular indicative present cuido, past participle cuidáu)

  1. to think, believe
    Synonyms: pensar, cuntar
    Cuida que van a dexalu solu
    He thinks they are going to leave him alone
    Cuido que ye verdá
    I think it's true
    • 1842, José Napoleón Acebal Morán, Los Trataos:
      Señor, fó que yo cudié que era una chancia el regalu
      Sir, it was me who thought the gift was a joke
    • 1861, Evanxeliu según San Marcos:
      Non cuidéis que yo vieni desfacer la llei, nin los profetas: non vieni desfacélos, sinon dáyos complimientu:
      Do not think that I came to undo the Law, nor the prophets: I did not come to undo them, but to make sure they are followed:
  2. to lie in wait
    Cuidarélu a la salida’l trabayu pa da-y el recáu
    I waited for him by his job's exit to give him the task
  3. to spy
    Synonym: esclucar
  4. to be careful [with, using something, to conserve it for example] (often with por)
    Synonym: mirar
    Dempués de la guerra cuidaron muncho pol aceite
    After the war, they took great care [to not waste] oil
  5. to take care (of someone, something)
    Synonym: curiar
  6. (reflexive) to make an effort
  7. (reflexive) to give oneself a good life

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin cogitāre. Compare Old Occitan cuidar, Middle French cuider, Spanish cuidar. Doublet of cogitar, a borrowing from Latin.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [kujˈða]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [kujˈðaɾ]
  • Audio (Barcelona):(file)
  • Rhymes: -a(ɾ)

Verb

[edit]

cuidar (first-person singular present cuido, first-person singular preterite cuidí, past participle cuidat)

  1. to think, to believe
  2. to be about to do something, especially having an accident
  3. to care for, to take care of

Old Spanish

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • cudar, cuedar, cueidar, cuydar, cueydar

Etymology

[edit]

    From earlier *coidar, from Latin cōgitāre (“to think”).[1]

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈkui̯ˈdaɾ/

    Verb

    [edit]

    cuidar

    1. (transitive) to think, believe [12th c.][2]
    2. (transitive) to look after, take care of [14th c.][2]

    Descendants

    [edit]
    • Ladino: kuidar / קואידאר
    • Spanish: cuidar

    Portuguese

    [edit]

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • cuydar (obsolete)

    Etymology

    [edit]

    From Old Galician-Portuguese cuidar, from Latin cōgitāre (“to think, to consider”), from co- + agitō (“to agitate”). Doublet of cogitar, a borrowing.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
     
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /kujˈda(ʁ)/ [kuɪ̯ˈda(h)]
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /kujˈda(ʁ)/ [kuɪ̯ˈda(h)]
      • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /kujˈda(ɾ)/ [kuɪ̯ˈda(ɾ)]
      • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /kujˈda(ʁ)/ [kuɪ̯ˈda(χ)]
      • (Caipira) IPA(key): /kujˈda(ɻ)/ [kuɪ̯ˈda(ɻ)]
     
    • (Portugal) IPA(key): /kujˈdaɾ/ [kujˈðaɾ]
    • (Portugal) IPA(key): /kujˈdaɾ/ [kujˈðaɾ]
      • (Southern Portugal) IPA(key): /kujˈda.ɾi/ [kujˈða.ɾi]

    • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
    • Audio (Portugal):(file)
    • Hyphenation: cui‧dar

    Verb

    [edit]

    cuidar (first-person singular present cuido, first-person singular preterite cuidei, past participle cuidado)

    1. (transitive) to take care (of); to look after (to provide care for) [with de]
      A mãe cuida das crianças. ― The mother tends the children.
    2. (intransitive) to take care; to be careful
    3. (transitive) to take care (of); to deal (with); to handle [with de]
      Não te preocupes, cuidarei deste problema. ― Don’t worry, I’ll take care of this problem.
    4. (transitive) to mind (to concern oneself with, to pay attention to) [with de]
      Cuida da tua vida! ― Mind your own business! (literally, “Mind your life!”)
    5. (transitive, archaic, dialectal) to think, to suppose to, to believe [with que]
    6. (reflexive) to take care (be cautious, careful)
    7. (reflexive, imperative) take care (used as a farewell)

    Spanish

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]
    Etymology tree

    Proto-Indo-European *ḱóm
    Proto-Italic *kom
    Proto-Italic *kom-

    Spanish cuidar

      Inherited from Old Spanish cuidar (“to think; to take care of”), from Latin cogitāre (“to think”).[1]

      Doublet of cogitar, a learned borrowing from Latin, whence also English cogitate.

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • IPA(key): /kwiˈdaɾ/ [kwiˈð̞aɾ]
      • Audio:(file)
      • Rhymes: -aɾ
      • Syllabification: cui‧dar

      Verb

      [edit]

      cuidar (first-person singular present cuido, first-person singular preterite cuidé, past participle cuidado)

      1. (ambitransitive) to look after, take care of (e.g. a house, a person) [transitive or with de ‘of’]
        La canguro está cuidando de mi hija.
        The babysitter is looking after my daughter.
      2. (transitive) to mind, watch, pay attention to, be mindful of
        Cuide su lenguaje.
        Watch your language.
      3. (reflexive) to look after oneself, take care
        cuídate ― take care
      4. (reflexive) to be careful of, watch out for [with de (+ infinitive) ‘of’]
        Cuídate de no contar mi secreto.
        Be careful not to spread my secret.
      5. (transitive, Costa Rica, rustic) to feed (an animal)[2]
